AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental trajectory is genuinely strong: Q1 FY2026 delivered +15.7% YoY revenue growth, +18.3% EPS growth, ~130bp gross margin expansion to 48.2%, and operating cash flow nearly doubling to $53.92B. Services hit a record $30B at 76.5% gross margin, and the 2.35B+ device installed base underpins durable recurring revenue. The balance sheet is deleveraging (debt down 6.6% YoY, equity up 32.1%). Valuation has compressed meaningfully — PE of 34.4x sits in the lower half of its 365-day range (30.2–43.1x), down ~8 points from the December 2025 peak despite accelerating earnings. However, the stock is not cheap in absolute terms: a 2.9% earnings yield vs 4.34% risk-free rate implies a negative equity-risk premium, and the multiple still demands sustained double-digit growth. The CEO transition (Tim Cook to John Ternus, announced 2026-04-20) is a near-term catalyst — timing one week before earnings signals management confidence in Q2 results, and Bank of America expects a $100B buyback authorization and 5% dividend increase on April 30. China iPhone shipments surged 20% YoY in Q1 2026, and the foldable iPhone is on track for September 2026. Offsetting risks include DOJ antitrust trial (late 2026), tariff exposure (~$5.6B annualized), and AI execution lag vs peers. The franchise is elite and the trajectory is accelerating, but the valuation leaves limited margin of safety — hence a moderate positive score rather than a strong one.
